extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO/OPAP staff handling application correspondence
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/processing requirements for submitting correspondence, drawings, signatures, facsimile transmissions, hand-delivery, and post-allowance papers to the USPTO (including special procedures for CPAs and national-stage EFS submissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper identification on incoming papers
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence related to a national patent application already filed must include identification by application number or patent number and the filing date assigned by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items requested on incoming papers (form paragraph 5.01): 1) Application number (checked for accuracy, including series code and serial no.), 2) Art Unit number (copied from most recent Office communication), 3) Filing date, 4) Name of the examiner who prepared the most recent Office action, 5) Title of invention, 6) Confirmation number (see MPEP § 503). Any correspondence not containing the proper identification set forth in 37 CFR 1.5(a) will be returned to the sender. Minor obvious errors that the Office readily recognizes may be corrected by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred identifying indicia on drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: If identifying indicia are provided on drawings, they must be placed on the front of each sheet within the top margin in accordance with 37 CFR 1.84(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifying indicia should include the title of the invention, inventor’s name, application number, and confirmation number. If no application or confirmation number yet assigned, provide docket number (if any).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of replacement or new drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date must be identified as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification must be pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d). A cover letter identifying the drawings by application number should accompany replacement sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defer submitting additional papers until application number received
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of additional or supplemental papers on a newly filed application should be deferred until an application number has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents with no particular time/order requirements (e.g., certified copies of foreign documents, changes of power of attorney, changes in mailing address) should be filed with materials submitted in reply to statutory/regulatory requirements to avoid processing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand-delivery location and general restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: All official patent application-related correspondence must be hand-carried to the Customer Service Window in Alexandria, VA, except for specified exceptions and certain offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No official paper relating to a pending application may be personally delivered to a Technology Center (TC), except papers subject to a secrecy order or national security classified directed to Licensing and Review. Before hand-carrying to a specific office, call to obtain current location; hand-carried correspondence taken to Customer Service Window will be accepted and routed (may incur delay).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence types eligible for direct hand-delivery to specific offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain correspondence types may be hand-carried to the specific office that processes them rather than the Customer Service Window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and locations: Access requests to Certified Copy Center (CCC); Office of General Counsel (Room 10C18 Madison East); Secrecy Order and classified correspondence to Licensing and Review (Room 4B31 Knox Building); Expedited foreign filing license petitions to drop-off box at Knox Building guard station; Petitions to withdraw from issue to Office of Petitions (Madison West); Office of Enrollment & Discipline receptionist (Room 8C43-B Madison West); Office of Finance receptionist (Suite 300 Carlyle Place) — see MPEP for telephone numbers, hours, and special procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile transmissions: permitted types of correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where specifically prohibited, many types of correspondence may be transmitted by facsimile and will be accorded a receipt date when the complete transmission is received by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted examples (37 CFR 1.6(d) and MPEP): CPAs under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (design apps only), amendments, declarations, petitions, information disclosure statements (IDS), terminal disclaimers, notices of appeal and appeal briefs, requests for continued examination (RCEs) under 37 CFR 1.114, assignment documents, issue fee transmittals, and authorizations to charge deposit accounts. Each transmission session should be limited to correspondence for a single application or proceeding; include application number/control number on fax cover sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile transmissions: prohibited types of correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain documents may not be transmitted by facsimile and, if submitted, will not be accorded a date of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited items (per 37 CFR 1.6(d) and II (A-L)): certified documents required by statute (37 CFR 1.4(f)); national patent application specification and drawings for obtaining an application filing date (except CPA 1.53(d)); international application for patent; international design application; copy of international application and basic national fee to enter national stage; third-party submissions under 1.290; correspondence relating to registration/enrollment/disciplinary matters; color drawings submitted under specified CFRs (1.81, 1.83-1.85, 1.152, 1.165, 1.173, 1.437, 1.1026); requests for reexamination (1.510, 1.913); requests for supplemental examination (1.610); correspondence in applications subject to secrecy orders directly related to the secrecy content (37 CFR 5.1-5.5); correspondence for contested cases/trials before PTAB except where Board expressly authorizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile receipt date rule and certificate of transmission exception
rubrics_metrics.description: The receipt date for permitted facsimile correspondence is the date the complete transmission is received by an Office facsimile unit, except if received on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday the receipt date is the next succeeding business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Certificate of Transmission is available (for documents not proscribed by 37 CFR 1.8(a)(2)), a facsimile completed on a Friday night may be considered timely filed on Friday if it contains the Certificate of Transmission and complies with 37 CFR 1.8(a)(1)(i)(B) and (ii). Example provided of cross-timezone completion and resulting receipt date shift. The Office may require additional evidence to determine if transmission/receipt occurred on the date in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit facsimile session content and include application/control number
rubrics_metrics.description: Each fax transmission session should be limited to correspondence to be filed in a single application or proceeding, and the application number or control number should be entered as part of the sender's identification on the facsimile cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This facilitates proper processing and matching incoming papers with application files. Office often experiences difficulty matching papers when insufficient or erroneous information is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized facsimile number and permitted per-office exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: All patent application related correspondence transmitted by facsimile must be directed to the USPTO central facsimile number (571-273-8300), with limited, specified exceptions allowing certain types to be sent to other office-specific numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP lists per-office fax numbers and the specific types of correspondence allowed to each (e.g., PCT Help Desk, Office of Data Management, EBC, Assignment Recordation Branch, CRU, PTAB (only where expressly authorized), OGC, Solicitor, Licensing & Review, Office of Petitions, OED, Office of Finance, Public Records Division). All other types must go to the central number.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA (continued prosecution application) fax special procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (available for design applications only) may be transmitted by facsimile, but special procedures and limitations apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPAs transmitted by fax are not ordinarily entitled to a Certificate of Transmission; applicant must include authorization to charge the basic filing fee to a deposit account or credit card or the CPA will be treated as filed without the basic filing fee under 37 CFR 1.53(f). There is a special receipt procedure whereby the Office will fax back a receipt if applicant submits the Office receipt form along with the CPA filing. If the Office has no evidence of receipt, the transmitting party may petition the Director to accord the CPA a filing date, provided they promptly inform the Office, supply an additional copy, and include an attesting statement plus a copy of the sending unit’s report or other evidence created after transmission and within one business day; the Office may require additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition procedure for lost evidence of faxed national-stage correspondence (EFS submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office has no evidence of receipt of national stage correspondence submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system (EFS), the submitting party may petition the Director to accord the correspondence a receipt date as of the date it was officially submitted to the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must: (i) inform the Office promptly upon learning no evidence exists, (ii) supply an additional copy of the correspondence, (iii) include a statement attesting on personal knowledge or to the Director’s satisfaction that the correspondence was previously officially submitted, and (iv) supply a copy of an acknowledgment receipt generated by EFS or equivalent evidence confirming the submission. The Office may require additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements: original handwritten signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Each piece of correspondence filed in an application, patent file, or other proceeding that requires a person's signature must generally be an original handwritten signature personally signed in permanent dark ink or its equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a copy (photocopy or facsimile) is filed instead, the original should be retained as evidence of authenticity; if authenticity is questioned the Office may require the original. Design patent practitioners must indicate 'design' adjacent to their handwritten signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-signature (slash-signature) format and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An S-signature consists of a signature inserted between forward slash marks (e.g., /Dr. James T. Jones, Jr/) and may be used in paper, facsimile, or as an EFS attachment in lieu of a handwritten signature, subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-signature must consist only of letters and/or Arabic numerals with appropriate punctuation. A patent practitioner signing under § 1.33(b)(1) or (2) must supply their registration number as part of or adjacent to the S-signature (hash '#' allowed only before a registration number). A design patent practitioner must indicate 'design' adjacent to the last forward slash of their S-signature. The signer’s name must be presented in printed/typed form immediately below or adjacent to the S-signature and be specific enough to readily recognize the identity of the signer. Persons filing documents signed by another must retain evidence of authenticity and have a reasonable basis to believe the signature was actually inserted by that person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronically submitted signature representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system may be signed by a graphic representation of a handwritten signature or a graphic representation of an S-signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphic signature submissions must comply with the same substantive signature rules; certifications and retention of evidence of authenticity remain applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification obligations and sanctions for papers and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation of any paper to the Office (by signing, filing, submitting, or later advocating) constitutes a certification under § 11.18(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of § 11.18(b)(2) may result in sanctions under § 11.18(c); practitioners violating § 11.18(b) may be subject to disciplinary action (see § 11.18(d)). The person inserting an S-signature or graphic signature certifies that the signature is their own; those submitting documents signed by another must have a reasonable basis to believe the signature was actually inserted by that person and retain evidence of authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing instructions and prohibited 'Hold for Pickup' service
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be sent by U.S. Postal Service or hand-carried, but applicants are urged to file new patent applications and correspondence via EFS when permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the 'Hold for Pickup' service option for mail to the USPTO; the Office does not pick up mail from postal facilities and 'Hold for Pickup' mail will not reach the Office. See MPEP § 501 for Priority Mail Express addresses and MPEP § 502.05 for electronic filing encouragement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-allowance correspondence address and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: All post-allowance correspondence, except petitions under 37 CFR 1.313(c), should be addressed 'Mail Stop Issue Fee.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.313(c) to withdraw an application from issue after payment should be clearly marked and filed as a Web-based ePetition, hand-carried to Office of Petitions, or faxed to Office of Petitions. All other petitions faxed must be directed to central facsimile number (571-273-8300). Any paper filed after receiving the Issue notification should include the indicated patent number. File post-allowance correspondence prior to payment of the issue fee to ensure consideration before issuance; see MPEP § 2732 regarding patent term adjustment impact of submitting amendments after a notice of allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return and correction of insufficiently identified papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will return papers that cannot be matched to application files due to insufficient or erroneous identifying information, but may correct minor obvious errors that are readily recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This particularly affects amendments, powers of attorney, changes of address, status letters, and petitions. Inspect returned papers to ensure they bear an 'Office Date' stamp showing the date of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile transmission may reduce drawing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of drawings by facsimile may reduce their quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will generally print the drawings as received; consider submitting higher-quality originals when possible. See MPEP § 1834.01 for discussion concerning facsimile transmissions in PCT applications.
